reason: The defect is real. si_direct ('best', critical c_si) credits passive death-wish questions, so a learner can finish without ever asking about active thoughts of killing herself. That contradicts the case anchor and the ASQ/C-SSRS pattern of asking the passive and active items separately. But the reviewer's deletion introduces a new error and is incomplete; see problem.
evidence: Internal: M02 ll.593-617 (si_direct), 1029-1046 (gate requiresIntents si_direct), 1151-1160 (c_si), rubric anchor l.1229; M01 pg_interview Safety Questions (passive question first, then active). recall: C-SSRS screener Q1 vs Q2; ASQ.
problem: NOT a drop-in-only fix. Applied alone, the deletion breaks the case. The si_active gate (and g_si_mixed for Marcus) requires si_direct, so a learner who asks exactly the question the house pocket guide lists first ('Have you wished you would not wake up?', pg_interview Safety Questions) would get no match. Dana or Marcus would then withhold the passive ideation they actually have, which is unrealistic and teaches that the passive question fails. The deletion also leaves most passive patterns in si_direct: 'better off dead' (PHQ-9 item-9 wording), 'want to die', 'thoughts about death/not waking up', 'better off without', 'not worth living', 'what's the point of living', and 'wish you weren't here'. The required fix: move all passive-wish patterns into a new intent si_passive (quality partial); add si_passive to the gate's requiresIntents so the disclosure still unlocks; add si_passive to c_si.partialIfOnly so full critical credit needs an active-ideation question.

reason: The substance is right: withdrawal-threshold induction is standard, not universal; low-dose initiation is a recognised alternative; and fentanyl can precipitate withdrawal even at usual COWS thresholds. COWS (Wesson & Ling 2003) was not Fudala's instrument (recall; unverified). The reviewer's appended clause says 'these COWS scores' where the feedback has none, and 'accepted alternative' is a little strong. I rewrote it. Coordinator: the stem ('critical requirement ... clinical pearls from Fudala') and the key still present a threshold as universal and attribute it to Fudala. Rewording the stem to 'standard buprenorphine induction' is needed for full consistency.
evidence: recall: ASAM National Practice Guideline 2020 Focused Update (low-dose initiation); SAMHSA TIP 63 (2021); Wesson & Ling, J Psychoactive Drugs 2003 (COWS).
correction: For standard induction, buprenorphine — a high-affinity partial agonist — given to a patient not yet in withdrawal can displace full agonists and precipitate acute withdrawal. This threshold is general induction practice, not a Fudala 2003 finding; low-dose ('micro') initiation without a withdrawal period is a recognized alternative, and after fentanyl use precipitated withdrawal can occur even at COWS 8–12.
problem: The item presents a withdrawal threshold (COWS ≥8–12) as a universal 'critical requirement' and attributes it to Fudala 2003. It omits low-dose initiation and the fentanyl-era risk of precipitated withdrawal.
